name: Chen Yiy Fon
current_role: CEO and Executive Director, NagaCorp Ltd (HKEX: 3918), operator of NagaWorld casino resort in Phnom Penh
profile: Second son of NagaCorp founder Tan Sri Dr Chen Lip Keong (d. Dec 2023). A USC economics graduate, he joined NagaCorp's board in 2015, became CEO of operations in 2022 and group CEO from 10 Dec 2023, inheriting the largest single allocation (~8.3%) of NagaCorp shares. He also holds board roles at Malaysian listed firms FACB Industries, Karambunai Corp and Petaling Tin.
interesting_fact: Took over as group CEO of NagaCorp, Cambodia's exclusive Phnom Penh casino licence holder, the day after his father's death in December 2023; ranked No. 21 on Asia Gaming Brief's 2025 Asian Gaming Power 50.
deep_cut_fact: Graduated in economics from the University of Southern California in 2003 and also chairs Malaysian-listed FACB Industries.
notes: Low public profile; no personal social accounts found. Best route is via NagaCorp investor relations (Head of IR Gerard Chai).

name: Xia Chongyao
current_role: Chairman and actual controller, Ningbo Orient Wires & Cables Co. (东方电缆, SSE: 603606)
profile: Xia Chongyao (夏崇耀) controls Ningbo Orient Wires & Cables via Ningbo Orient Group; the company, founded in 1998 and listed in Shanghai in 2014, is one of China's leading makers of submarine power cables for offshore wind. He chairs the board and leads its push into deep-sea wind and overseas markets (UK subsidiary registered 2024).
interesting_fact: At the 2024 results call he said Orient's order book had hit RMB 17.98bn (up 130%), overseas revenue rose ~480% in 2024, and its umbilical cables are already used in 1,500m-deep offshore oil projects, replacing imports.
deep_cut_fact: Orient Cable's umbilical cable is a national 'single champion' (单项冠军) product; Xia has framed it as replacing previously imported equipment for China's deep-sea oil and gas.
notes: Highly relevant to energy (offshore wind/HVDC subsea cables). IR email is from a 2022 company filing; verify current address in latest annual report. Chinese-language outreach advised.

name: Robert Toennies
current_role: 50% shareholder, Tönnies Group (operating at holding level as Premium Food Group since Jan 2025), Rheda-Wiedenbrück
profile: Son of Tönnies co-founder Bernd Tönnies (d. 1994), Robert inherited a stake in Germany's largest meat processor, cofounded in 1971 by his father and uncle Clemens, and holds 50% of the group. The business, rebranded at holding level as Premium Food Group in 2025, has ~€8bn revenue and ~22,000 staff across meat, convenience, plant-based alternatives, pet food and logistics.
interesting_fact: From 1 January 2025 the Tönnies holding operates as the Premium Food Group, signalling a shift beyond meat into convenience, ingredients and plant-based alternatives; Robert was named among the shareholders backing the strategy.
notes: Very private; no personal accounts found. Group press office speaks mainly for the Clemens/Maximilian side; Robert has historically communicated via lawyers. Long-running family shareholder dispute is a sensitive topic — avoid. Group's energy/environmental management contact also listed on the same page.

name: Zhou Liangzhang
current_role: Founder and Chairman, Hexing Electrical Co. (海兴电力, SSE: 603556), Hangzhou
profile: Zhou Liangzhang (周良璋, b. 1963) worked at the state-owned Hangzhou Instrument Factory before founding Hexing in 1992. Hexing makes smart meters, metering/AMI systems, distribution equipment and new-energy solutions for power utilities, selling to 80+ countries; overseas business brought in RMB 2.94bn of 2024 revenue, with plants in Europe, Latin America and Africa.
interesting_fact: Hexing earns about two-thirds of its revenue abroad, building localised smart-meter factories in Europe, Latin America and Africa — an unusually global footprint for a Chinese grid-equipment maker.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding Hexing in 1992, Zhou was deputy head of the foreign-economic-relations office at the Hangzhou Instrument Factory and then general manager of Hangzhou Yida Industrial Instrument Manufacturing Co.
notes: Grid/smart-meter angle fits energy podcast. Board secretary (2024 report): Jin Yi. Chinese-language outreach via IR office recommended.

name: Somporn Juangroongruangkit
current_role: Chair/President, Thai Summit Group; director of Thai Summit Autoparts Industry Co.
profile: Somporn Juangroongruangkit (สมพร จึงรุ่งเรืองกิจ) took over Thai Summit Group, founded in 1977 by her late husband Phatana, and built it into one of Thailand's and ASEAN's largest auto-parts makers: 40+ companies, 26 factories in Thailand, Indonesia, India, China, Vietnam, Japan and the US, and revenue above US$2.6bn. Her children Sakulthorn and Chanapun now run day-to-day operations.
interesting_fact: In Feb 2026 Bloomberg reported global PE firms were circling Thai Summit at a possible $1.5–2bn valuation; the group publicly denied any sale, saying it was proud to be a Thai company with leading technology able to compete globally amid the EV transition.
deep_cut_fact: Thai Summit's flagship Thai Summit Autoparts Industry, on whose board she sits, has reported a profit every single year since 2005.
notes: Very low profile; mother of politician Thanathorn — politics is sensitive (company states politically active family members have no role in management). EV-transition angle for podcast. Route via Thai Summit corporate office.

name: Desmond Sacco
current_role: President, Assore Ltd (Johannesburg manganese, iron ore and chrome miner; joint owner of Assmang)
profile: Johannesburg-born geologist Desmond Sacco joined Assore, the mining group his father Guido founded in 1928, in 1968; he joined the board in 1974 and was chairman and MD from 1992, also chairing Assmang from 1999. Assore (manganese, iron ore, chrome) is now privately held; he is listed as President, with Patrick Sacco as executive chairman and Charles Walters as CEO.
interesting_fact: Holds a BSc in geology from Wits, where he played cricket and hockey, and is a fellow of the Geological Society of South Africa.
deep_cut_fact: He owns one of the world's great private collections of African minerals; the Mineralogical Record devoted a 2014 supplement, 'Des Sacco: A Few African Favorites', to it, and Rocks & Minerals profiled it in 2012.
notes: Very private; does not exhibit his collection publicly. Assore delisted from the JSE; contact via company. Mineral-collecting is the best personal hook.

name: Barry Canton
current_role: Co-founder and Chief Technology Officer, Ginkgo Bioworks (NYSE: DNA), Boston
profile: Dublin-born engineer Barry Canton co-founded Ginkgo Bioworks in 2009 with MIT classmates Jason Kelly, Reshma Shetty and Austin Che and professor Tom Knight, building a platform for programming cells by rewriting DNA. As CTO he leads Ginkgo's foundry technology strategy; the company went public via SPAC in 2021 and is now pushing autonomous labs and AI models trained on biological data.
interesting_fact: Grew up in Sutton, north Dublin, studied mechanical engineering at UCD (working on biomechanics of head injuries) and made the 'unusual transition' to biological engineering with a PhD at MIT, which he started in 2003 aged 23.
deep_cut_fact: Explains Ginkgo's thesis as 'all of biology runs on digital code... DNA and the four letters ACGT'; his UCD research on skull injuries is what first got him interested in applying engineering principles to biology.
notes: Billionaire status was at 2021-22 peak; Ginkgo stock has fallen sharply since, so net worth likely well below $1B now. Has done tech/AI podcasts (e.g., Turing Post on DNA language models) — good fit for data/AI angle. Route via Ginkgo press office.
